beats.narration: If Earth suddenly stopped spinning, even for one second, everything not bolted down would keep flying east at about a thousand miles an hour.

shots.scene_description: Earth spinning in space then abruptly stopping, 1,000 MPH label
The man in the blue hoodie flung sideways through the air with speed lines

beats.narration: That's because right now, at the equator, you're already moving that fast. You just can't feel it, because everything around you moves with you.

shots.scene_description: Earth with glowing equator, a tiny figure riding the surface, speed readout
The man standing calmly, clouds and trees drifting together with him

beats.narration: So when the ground stops, you don't. Neither do cars, trees, houses, or even the air.

shots.scene_description: Street scene: car, tree and house sliding east with motion lines
Close-up of the car tumbling past with debris

beats.narration: The atmosphere would keep racing along at supersonic speed, creating winds stronger than any tornado, scraping across the whole planet.

shots.scene_description: Trees bent flat under huge wind streaks
Earth wrapped in roaring white wind bands

beats.narration: The oceans would keep moving too, sending giant walls of water miles inland.

shots.scene_description: A towering wave rising over a coastal city
The wave crashing over the buildings

beats.narration: And if Earth stayed stopped, things get even weirder. One day would last a whole year: about six months of sunlight, then six months of darkness.

shots.scene_description: Earth and Sun, one side lit, 1 DAY = 1 YEAR
Sky over a house shifting from day to long night with a month counter

beats.narration: Without the spin, the oceans would slowly flow toward the poles, and a giant new continent would rise around the middle of the planet.

shots.scene_description: Earth with water creeping to the poles
A huge brown continent band appearing around the equator

beats.narration: But here's the crazy part. Earth actually is slowing down, right now.

shots.scene_description: A speedometer for Earth whose needle is dropping
Clock with NOW label

beats.narration: When dinosaurs were alive, a day was about half an hour shorter. The Moon's pull is gently putting on the brakes.

shots.scene_description: A dinosaur under the sun with a 23.5 HOURS clock
The Moon tugging on Earth's ocean bulge like a brake

beats.narration: Don't worry though. Each century, our day only gets about two thousandths of a second longer. So hold on tight... we're still spinning.

shots.scene_description: Tiny stopwatch: +0.002 seconds per century
The man relieved, waving, Earth spinning happily behind him
